facts.text: SoftGym is a set of benchmark environments for deformable object manipulation built on the Nvidia FleX simulator with a standard Gym API
The README documents compiling PyFleX with CMake and Pybind11
FlexEnv is a gym.Env, the legacy Gym API
FlexEnv imports pyflex and raises gym.error.DependencyNotInstalled when the compiled binding is missing
PourWaterPosControlEnv extends FluidEnv
FluidEnv extends FlexEnv
PourWaterPosControlEnv accepts the observation modes cam_rgb, point_cloud and key_point and the action modes rotation_bottom and rotation_top
The key_point observation has 13 elements: the two cups' positions and shapes, the water height and the water fractions of the two cups
The key_point observation space is a Box of 13 values bounded by -inf and +inf
In the rotation_bottom and rotation_top action modes the action space is a 3-element Box: (dx, dy) for the floor centre and dtheta for its rotation
The key_point observation is built from the glass pose and shape, the poured glass pose and shape, the water height and the two water fractions
The reward is the fraction of water particles inside the poured glass and outside the control glass
The reward range is 0 to 1
FlexEnv's default action_repeat is 8
FlexEnv.step calls _step once per action_repeat before it computes the observation and reward
FlexEnv.step increments time_step and marks the episode done when time_step reaches the horizon
FlexEnv.step returns the legacy four-value (observation, reward, done, info) tuple
FlexEnv's default horizon is 100
The PourWaterPosControl-v0 registration sets the horizon to 75
The PourWaterPosControl-v0 registration passes action_mode='direct'
The class itself only accepts action_mode rotation_bottom or rotation_top, so the registered value 'direct' fails its assertion
PourWaterPosControl-v0 is registered with entry point softgym.envs.pour_water:PourWaterPosControlEnv
FluidEnv.set_scene creates the fluid scene with pyflex.set_scene
FlexEnv.reset loads a cached configuration and state and returns only the observation

determinism.notes: reset(seed) seeds the fake's placeholder start state, and cap.world.seed.v1 supplies the seed of the next reset.  The upstream environment is created with deterministic=True, which selects cached configuration 0 (flex_env.py:158-161); its cached scene variations are generated with numpy's global generator (pour_water.py:111-127), while the fake uses Python's random.Random, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two.  There is no wall-clock pacing.

gaps: F0 analytic stand-in: the fake models the pouring glass pose and two scalar water fractions directly; there is no fluid particle simulation, no contact or collision handling, no friction, no pyflex and therefore no claim about forces or fluid dynamics
only the key_point observation is served: the cam_rgb image (720 x 720 x 3, pour_water.py:44-45) and the point_cloud particle array are not modelled, and cap.world.render.v1 is unbound
the fake does not load the cached start-state pickle of pour_water.py:31; its start pose and glass dimensions are placeholders, not the environment's cached scene

no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and timestep_ms 0, because the clone exposes no fixed physics timestep in Python; one cap.world.step.v1 tick is one FlexEnv.step, which repeats the action action_repeat (default 8) times (flex_env.py:177-181)
the legacy four-value step return (flex_env.py:197) has one done flag, not terminated/truncated: the bridge serves the horizon case (flex_env.py:192-194) as terminated=True and truncated=False
snapshot and restore are not offered: FlexEnv and PourWaterPosControlEnv define get_state/set_state (pour_water.py:161-187), but the fake does not implement them, so snapshot_restore is false
the sim backend was not run: it needs PyFlex compiled (README.md:22) and register_flex_envs() called (the clone defines it at softgym/__init__.py:9 but never calls it)
no physical device is modelled: SoftGym is a simulator and the model was never validated against hardware

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
